title: Sentence role-tagging classifier (direct answer / supporting evidence / background / contradiction)
goal: Replace the current binary found/missing/conflicted status (lab/common/verify.coverage_check) with a 4-way role label per shortlisted sentence -- direct_answer, supporting_evidence, background, contradiction -- so the page-wise writer knows how to use each sentence.
method: Multinomial logistic regression (sklearn), trained on 480 scenarios generated by construction (4 roles x 120 each, so the gold label is known with certainty, the same approach EXP-011 uses for its own labels) across 4 slot/value fixtures plus a small background-sentence pool. Features: lexical NLI entail/neutral/contradict probability (lab.common.nli.judge) between the candidate sentence and a claim built from the ask, ask-relevance coverage (lab.common.relevance.ask_relevance), and a synthetic sentence-position value. 75/25 train/test split, stratified.
results_prose: 4-way role classifier: test accuracy 1.0 on 120 held-out items (360 training). Per-role accuracy: direct_answer=1.0, supporting_evidence=1.0, background=1.0, contradiction=1.0. Confusion matrix: {'direct_answer': {'direct_answer': 30, 'supporting_evidence': 0, 'background': 0, 'contradiction': 0}, 'supporting_evidence': {'direct_answer': 0, 'supporting_evidence': 30, 'background': 0, 'contradiction': 0}, 'background': {'direct_answer': 0, 'supporting_evidence': 0, 'background': 30, 'contradiction': 0}, 'contradiction': {'direct_answer': 0, 'supporting_evidence': 0, 'background': 0, 'contradiction': 30}}.
conclusion: The three features separate all four roles cleanly on this generated set: NLI entailment isolates direct_answer, NLI contradiction isolates contradiction, and ask-relevance coverage is what actually separates supporting_evidence from background -- a distinction NLI alone cannot make, since both score near-neutral against the direct claim. This is the real reason EXP-049's relevance score is a load-bearing input feature here, not an optional extra.
scale_down: Labels are generated by construction from 4 slot/value fixtures and a 4-sentence background pool, not from a real document's actual shortlist -- the classifier has not been measured on real documents' sentences, only on this synthetic set. The position feature is a random float with no relationship to role in this generated set (a real pipeline's shortlist would have a real position-to-role correlation this fixture cannot represent), so this run cannot say whether position actually helps versus being inert; the model may be relying on it by chance. supporting_evidence/background are each drawn from a small fixed sentence template/pool, not a broad distribution of real phrasings.
follow_ups: Measure against a real document's actual shortlisted sentences (not generated-by-construction labels) once a labeled real-document fixture exists, to check whether accuracy holds outside this generated set's narrow phrasing.
models_used: Multinomial logistic regression (sklearn), the same head shape as EXP-011's next_action_head. Features come from lab.common.nli.judge (lexical, deterministic) and lab.common.relevance.ask_relevance (lexical, deterministic). No generative model, no neural encoder.
